blocks.x: Edge Computing & Distributed Infrastructure as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

When the decision lives at the machine — a vision inspection, a grid relay setting, a store kiosk — the cloud round trip is the architecture mistake. We engineer edge estate: hardware selection and sizing for the environment (IP-rated, DIN-rail, GPU-capable), KubeEdge/K3s-class orchestration with fleet management, offline-first application patterns, model deployment pipelines with OTA updates, and store-and-forward telemetry that survives connectivity loss.

Security gets specific at the edge: physical tamper considerations, hardware roots of trust, signed images and measured boot, and network segmentation aligned to IEC 62443 zones-and-conduits for industrial estates. Fleet operations are the real product — thousands of nodes versioned, monitored and updated like a software estate, with SLOs per site.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
